new.s: Mangal Pandey, who attacked British officers at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857, belonged to which unit?
new.x: Mangal Pandey was a sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry at Barrackpore. He acted on 29 March 1857 and was executed on 8 April 1857. The 3rd Light Cavalry was the unit at Meerut, the 1st Cavalry of the Hyderabad Contingent was disarmed at Aurangabad in June 1857, and the 19th Native Infantry was a separate unit.

new.x: The Government of India Act, 1858, passed after the Revolt, ended Company rule and vested India in the Crown. The Charter Act 1853 and Pitt's India Act 1784 left the Company in place, and the Indian Councils Act 1861 came after the transfer.

new.x: Lord Canning read the Proclamation at a Durbar in Allahabad on 1 November 1858 (UPPSC 2009). Delhi is the venue of the 1877 Durbar that proclaimed Victoria Empress of India. Calcutta and Lucknow were not the venue, and the dates in A and D are wrong.

new.s: Queen Victoria became 'Empress of India' in:
o: 1858, under the Government of India Act, 1858
1877, under the Royal Titles Act 1876, proclaimed at the Delhi Durbar under Lytton
1911, at the Delhi Durbar of George V
new.x: The Royal Titles Act 1876 gave Victoria the title, and it was proclaimed at the Delhi Durbar of 1 January 1877 under Lord Lytton. The 1858 Act only transferred power to the Crown; some notes wrongly place the title at the 1858 Allahabad Durbar. The 1861 Act and the 1911 Durbar have nothing to do with the title.
new.tq: Empress of India = 1877 (Act of 1876), Lytton, Delhi.

new.s: The Brahmo Sabha, founded in Calcutta in 1828 and later renamed the Brahmo Samaj, was founded by:
new.x: Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in August 1828 with Dwarkanath Tagore (APPSC-GS 2018). It grew out of his Atmiya Sabha of 1815. Dayananda founded the Arya Samaj (1875). Ramakrishna was a mystic, not the founder of a Samaj, and Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897).
